newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine dealers see no market impact from sackings.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine dealers see no market impact from sackings.

text.p: The dismissal of Ukraine's finance and economy ministers will have no immediate impact on the former Soviet republic's currency and Treasury bill markets, dealers said on Wednesday.

Finance Minister Valentyn Koronevsky, sacked by President Leonid Kuchma for "serious inadequacies in his work," did not play an active role in deciding the finance ministry's T-bill policy, dealers said.

"In time, when someone else is appointed to the post of finance minister, the ministry's T-bill policy could change. But now, it is hard to guess whether the market will grow or freeze," Bank of Ukraine chief dealer Olexander Samoilov said.
He was speaking after Kuchma sacked Koronevsky, Economy Minister Vasyl Hureyev, Statistics Minister Olexander Osaulenko and the minister for machine-building and the military complex.
The hryvnia fell to 1.8360 per dollar on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange on Wednesday from 1.8150 on Tuesday.
It fell sharply at the start of the week from Friday's near record 1.7650 on what the central bank attributed to commercial banks' speculative dollar withholding.
In recent weeks, the hryvnia has strengthened on heavy non-resident buying of Ukraine's high-yielding T-bills.

One dealer, who asked not to be named, recalled that markets were sensitive to central bank Chief Viktor Yushchenko's reappointment last month because he was a prominent advocate of tight monetary policy.
But analysts say Kuchma, Prime Minster Pavlo Lazarenko, Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk and Yushchenko control economic and financial policy.

Analysts' reactions to the sackings were overall negative, but they agreed economic policy would probably not undergo drastic changes and suggested the move was designed to protect Lazarenko's position.
Non-residents have become so active in Ukraine's high-yield T-bill market that they helped push the hryvnia currency up to near-record highs of 1.765 last week.
